themes.consensus_view: Banks treat the AI spending boom as the main engine of 2026 markets and keep raising their spending forecasts, with the open question being how the buildout gets funded, since debt, company balance sheets, and electricity supply come up repeatedly and no desk in this set argues the boom is ending.

facts_agreed.claim: AI capital spending is the central driver of the 2026 market backdrop, with datacenter and infrastructure buildout referenced across desks.
evidence_quotes: The dominant feature of the investment landscape in 2026 remains the remarkable boom in AI investment

facts_agreed.claim: How the buildout gets financed, and whether it earns a return, is a live concern rather than a settled question.
evidence_quotes: AI-related capex and balance sheet risk

facts_agreed.claim: Physical and cost inputs to the buildout, chiefly power supply and the price of compute, are tracked as binding constraints on how far spending can run.
evidence_quotes: AI data center power supply constraints

facts_agreed.claim: The buildout extends down the supply chain into semiconductor manufacturing capacity and compute deployment.

themes.consensus_view: Banks agree the big cloud companies are spending far more on AI data centers than Wall Street had penciled in, but they split hard on whether that spending pays off or becomes the first real overinvestment bust since 2008, with credit markets already charging more to fund it.

facts_agreed.claim: Hyperscalers are still raising AI spending plans, and the banks think street forecasts are behind the actual pace.
evidence_quotes: Consensus 2027 capex is too low…we model 54% growth for GOOG/L
hyperscalers continue to invest aggressively because they are confident that their unprecedented spending on AI will pay off

facts_agreed.claim: Goldman argues the market is undervaluing the cash flow and core-business payoff the hyperscalers are already getting from AI compute.
evidence_quotes: market underestimates how much future cash flow Msft, Amzn and Google will generate
solid indicator of the application of AI compute to the company’s core business
we maintain our conviction that current stock performance underestimates META’s ability to scale

facts_agreed.claim: Desks treat hyperscaler capex as the swing factor for the broad equity tape right now.
evidence_quotes: we maintain our Tactically Bullish call flagging hyperscaler capex as a datapoint
the stall in the S&P 500 rally we have experienced for the better part of two months

facts_contested.claim: whether the AI capex boom pays off or is overinvestment
facts_contested.for_evidence: we believe this point in time represents an unusually attractive buying opportunity
facts_contested.against_evidence: For the first time since the GFC, we have a clear candidate for overinvestment

facts_contested.claim: whether debt-funded AI buildout is a real credit risk
facts_contested.for_evidence: market underestimates how much future cash flow Msft, Amzn and Google will generate
facts_contested.against_evidence: The CDS market is charging for it.

themes.consensus_view: Four desks treat Fed policy under Chair Warsh as a live macro driver this window, but they read his signal in opposite ways — one calls his framework hawkish (leaning toward higher rates), another heard dovish (leaning toward easier policy) tones at his press conference — so no agreed direction has been staked.

facts_agreed.claim: Four banks flag Fed policy and communication under Chair Warsh as a live macro subject this window, referencing it in context rather than staking a directional call.
evidence_quotes: Chairman Warsh's press conference dovish signals
Fed interest rate policy under Warsh

facts_agreed.claim: Warsh's own credibility and how he communicates policy are treated as part of the story, not just the rate decision itself.
evidence_quotes: Fed post-Fed setup and Warsh credibility

facts_contested.claim: how to read Warsh's policy signal — hawkish framework versus dovish press-conference tone
facts_contested.against_evidence: Chairman Warsh's press conference dovish signals

themes.consensus_view: Four desks keep pointing at the Strait of Hormuz — the shipping chokepoint that moves a big slice of the world's oil and gas — as a live risk to energy supply, but none of them has committed to a call on whether it closes, reopens, or stays jammed.

facts_agreed.claim: Four banks flag the Strait of Hormuz as an active supply and shipping risk this window, referencing it in context without taking a directional side.
evidence_quotes: Strait of Hormuz energy supply disruption

themes.consensus_view: Goldman, JPMorgan and MUFG all reference renewed US-Iran military escalation as a live backdrop for oil and risk assets this window, but none of them stakes out a directional call on where it goes next.

facts_agreed.claim: Three banks flag US-Iran military escalation and Middle East hostilities as an active macro backdrop this window, treating it as context rather than a directional trade.

themes.consensus_view: Every desk covering this agrees memory stocks have been sold off to the point of capitulation (holders giving up and dumping), but only The Market Ear takes the next step and argues the selling has now reached chart support levels where pressing fresh bets on further downside gets expensive.

facts_agreed.claim: Memory stocks have been hit by a broad, heavy round of selling that desks describe as a washout rather than ordinary rotation.
Memory pricing itself is the variable desks are tracking underneath the selloff.
The major memory names have fallen to significant technical support, which makes new short positions less attractive.
evidence_quotes: nearly every major memory name is sitting on significant support

themes.consensus_view: Every desk in this window treats the chip and AI-datacenter spending boom as the market's central story, but only one of them actually stakes a view that the spending holds up, while the rest just track how big it is, how it is being paid for, and whether it earns its money back.

How the spending is financed, and what it does to corporate balance sheets, is a live concern rather than an afterthought.

evidence_quotes: Semiconductor capex remains his highest-conviction theme, given its more durable competitive advantages
